title: First-open substitution for the specified relative product
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p_0,\ell$, integers $d,n\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p_0^d}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Work with a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] and the specified canonical exchange and projection maps [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Write $P_h=Lh^*$, $S_h=Rh_!$ and $J_i=i_!$ for an open immersion; for proper $h$ use $S_h=Rh_*$. All tensors are derived over $\Lambda$, and $\sigma$ is the signed symmetry. Use the canonical composition comparisons $\alpha_{h,e}:S_hS_e\cong S_{he}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition], on the bounded constructible etale-origin domain identified by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. For $A$ on the target of $h$ and $N$ on its source, put $\Theta_h(A,N)=S_h(\sigma)\operatorname{PF}_{h,N,A}\sigma:A\otimes S_hN\to S_h(P_hA\otimes N)$. For $h:V\to B$, $z:Z\to B$, projections $r_0:V\times_BZ\to V$, $s_0:V\times_BZ\to Z$, and $C\in D^b_{ctf}(V,\Lambda)$, $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$, define the specified map
$$\lambda_{h,z}(C,N)=\alpha_{z,s_0}\,S_z\bigl(\operatorname{PF}_{s_0,P_{r_0}C,N}(\operatorname{Ex}_{h,z}(C)\otimes1)\bigr)\Theta_z(S_hC,N).$$
Juxtaposition composes right to left, with the canonical pullback and tensor associators inserted. Let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ be open, $a:\bar X\to B$ proper and $g:Y\to B$ any such morphism. Put $f=aj$, $T=X\times_BY$, $U=\bar X\times_BY$, with projections $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to Y$, $r:U\to\bar X$, $s:U\to Y$, and $v=j\times_B1_Y:T\hookrightarrow U$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, put $D=P_pK\otimes P_qL$. Let $\beta:P_rJ_jK\xrightarrow{\sim}J_vP_pK$ be the open-unit-normalized base-change map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and define
$$e_1=\operatorname{PF}_{v,P_pK,P_sL}(\beta\otimes1):P_rJ_jK\otimes P_sL\xrightarrow{\sim}J_vD.$$
This is the one-open external tensor map of [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization]. Under $S_{aj}\cong S_aJ_j$ and $S_q\cong S_sJ_v$, one has the identities of specified morphisms
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{aj,g}(K)=S_s(\beta)\operatorname{Ex}_{a,g}(J_jK),\qquad
\lambda_{aj,g}(K,L)=S_gS_s(e_1)\lambda_{a,g}(J_jK,L).$$
The latter target is identified with $S_{gq}D$ by the indicated composition comparisons.

proof.text: Work at the fixed finite coefficient ring. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], the bounded constructible inputs have etale-origin witnesses, so the composition comparisons of [thm-sf-comp-composition] apply on the stipulated domain. Put $M=P_pK$, $F=P_rJ_jK$, $H=P_sL$ and $E=\operatorname{Ex}_{a,g}(J_jK)$. The normalized open base change of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] is $\beta:F\to J_vM$. Its open tensor map is $\operatorname{PF}_{v,M,H}:J_vM\otimes H\to J_v(M\otimes P_vH)$. Since $sv=q$, the specified pullback comparison identifies $P_vH=P_qL$. Thus the composite $\operatorname{PF}_{v,M,H}(\beta\otimes1)$ is exactly $e_1$, including its open-unit normalization, by [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization] with its second open immersion equal to the identity.

proof.text: Paste vertically the open Cartesian square $(p,v,j,r)$ and the proper Cartesian square $(r,s,a,g)$. Clause 2 of [fix-lem-exchanges] gives, through the composition comparisons, $\operatorname{Ex}_{aj,g}(K)=S_s(\operatorname{Ex}_{j,r}(K))E$. In [def-exchange-projection], choose the compactification of the open $j$ whose proper factor is the identity. Its proper factor is the direct-image exchange of [def-exchange-projection] for the square $(1,1,r,r)$ whose vertical arrows are identities: there $\eta_{1}$ and $\varepsilon_{1}$ are identities and $\theta$ is the canonical comparison for $r\circ1=1\circ r$, so this factor is the identity under the canonical identity-functor comparisons. Hence the compactification formula identifies $\operatorname{Ex}_{j,r}(K)$ with the canonical open base-change map. For our constant finite ring this is precisely $\beta$ by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Clause 4 of [fix-lem-exchanges] ensures this identification uses the canonical compact-support comparisons. We obtain the first claimed identity, not merely an unspecified isomorphism.

proof.text:
Apply the composition pentagon of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] to $T\xrightarrow{v}U\xrightarrow{s}Y$ and the inputs $(M,L)$. Its explicit equality is
$$\operatorname{PF}_{q,M,L}(\alpha_{s,v,M}\otimes1)=\alpha_{s,v,D}\,S_s(\operatorname{PF}_{v,M,H})\operatorname{PF}_{s,J_vM,L}.$$
Naturality in the first input, applied to $\beta:F\to J_vM$, also gives
$$\operatorname{PF}_{s,J_vM,L}(S_s\beta\otimes1)=S_s(\beta\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{s,F,L}.$$
The first identity of step 2, before suppressing composition comparisons, reads $\operatorname{Ex}_{aj,g}(K)=\alpha_{s,v,M}S_s(\beta)E$. Substitute this and the naturality equality into the pentagon, and combine the two factors inside $S_s$ using its functoriality and the definition of $e_1$. This yields
$$\operatorname{PF}_{q,M,L}(\operatorname{Ex}_{aj,g}(K)\otimes1)=\alpha_{s,v,D}\,S_s(e_1)\operatorname{PF}_{s,F,L}(E\otimes1).$$
Both sides start at $P_gS_{aj}K\otimes L$, read as $P_gS_aJ_jK\otimes L$.

proof.text:
Expand the definition of $\lambda_{aj,g}$ from the statement and substitute step 3 inside $S_g$. Naturality of the projection transformation, asserted by [prop-sf-pf-coherence], and naturality of the signed symmetry identify its first factor $\Theta_g(S_{aj}K,L)$ with $\Theta_g(S_aJ_jK,L)$ under $\alpha_{a,j,K}$. For the last factor use the associativity clause of [thm-sf-comp-composition]:
$$\alpha_{g,q,D}\,S_g(\alpha_{s,v,D})=\alpha_{gs,v,D}\,(\alpha_{g,s,J_vD}).$$
Naturality of $\alpha_{g,s}$ moves $S_gS_s(e_1)$ across this comparison. The remaining factors are exactly $\alpha_{g,s}S_g(\operatorname{PF}_{s,F,L}(E\otimes1))\Theta_g(S_aJ_jK,L)=\lambda_{a,g}(J_jK,L)$. Hence, with the target comparison stipulated in the statement,
$$\lambda_{aj,g}(K,L)=S_gS_s(e_1)\lambda_{a,g}(J_jK,L).$$
The calculation neither interchanges tensor factors nor introduces an additional symmetry, so the signs are precisely those already present in $\Theta_g$.
